baseline.holdoutRule: All previously exposed images, including the four v21 holdouts, are regression cases. After candidate code and labels are frozen, select new pixel-reviewed holdouts with at least two return_point truths and at least two non-return_point truths. Each holdout must pass every classification, action and safety assertion with zero provider errors. Apply the ordered v22 container-category rules to the submitted pixels. Image exactness remains at least 95%, return-point recall at least 90%, and wrong non-null channels and false return points remain zero tolerance. Reject near-duplicate source pairs at 0.995 before any model call. These checks are developer-visible, frozen and non-adaptive, not sealed blind tests.

invariants: Route a single intact, uncontaminated prepackaged plastic or metal drink bottle, can or cup to return_point by container category. Capacity only excludes: a stated or visible capacity outside 150ml-3L routes to blue_bin, and an unknown capacity withholds nothing.
The S$0.10 refund requires purchase in Singapore and the Deposit Mark; the machine scans the product barcode and decides acceptance.
A readable 10¢ SG RETURN mark on the drink container fills only an unknown shape or material, never known exclusions.
Observed contamination takes priority over damage, out-of-range volume and explicit text exclusions; these route to general_waste and blue_bin respectively.
Glass, cartons, pouches, non-beverages, powdered drinks, food for special medical purposes and freshly prepared drinks are outside the deposit category.
Multiple containers, outer packaging and scenes without an identifiable container stay not_sure with no action.

actual.reason: This is a composite/paper beverage carton (Tetra Pak type). Cartons are NOT eligible for BCRS return_point regardless of contents. Under NEA guidelines, clean and dry Tetra Pak / milk cartons go in the blue bin.
preparation: Rinse out any remaining oat milk
Ensure the carton is clean and dry
Flatten if possible to save space
actual.tip: Cartons and pouches are excluded from the BCRS scheme. If your estate has a dedicated carton recycling collection, you may use that; otherwise the blue bin is correct.

actual.item: Dove Intense Repair Nourishing Shampoo bottle (80ml)
actual.reason: This is a personal care product (shampoo), not a beverage container. It is not eligible for BCRS return_point. The bottle is a small HDPE plastic container with a flip-top cap, typically used for non-beverage personal care products. While clean plastic bottles can sometimes go in blue_bin, this is a small personal care container with a mixed-material cap (plastic and possibly a metal spring in the flip mechanism), and shampoo residue makes it difficult to ensure clean and dry condition. NEA guidelines prioritize clean and dry recyclables for blue_bin. Given the product residue risk and small size with mixed components, general waste is the appropriate channel.
preparation: Ensure bottle is completely empty
Rinse thoroughly to remove shampoo residue
Remove and dispose of cap separately in general waste
If clean and dry, the empty bottle body may be placed in blue_bin; however due to residue risk, general waste is safer
actual.tip: For future purchases, consider buying larger refill sizes to reduce packaging waste, or look for brands offering refill stations.

actual.item: green Tetra Pak beverage carton (Fit Fresh, 250 ml)
actual.reason: Tetra Pak cartons are recyclable in Singapore's blue bin system. This is a composite paper-based carton, not a plastic or metal beverage container, so BCRS return_point does not apply.
preparation: Rinse out any remaining liquid
Flatten to save space
Place in blue recycling bin
actual.tip: Tetra Pak cartons are recycled through the blue bin, not the BCRS return system. Ensure it is clean and dry before recycling.
